The starting point

High-volume notifications deserve a faster, more consistent first decision.

Supplier change notifications arrive by email and require an initial assessment before the right operational path can begin. FLASH AI focuses the first automation on the supplier segment where scale and repeatability are already visible.

✉

What changed

Notifications are received centrally in the Bayer Pharma email box, creating a continuous intake stream that needs sorting before downstream work begins.

⌁

Why it matters

The top six suppliers account for about 1,200 SCNs per year—roughly half of the volume from 3,700 suppliers—and their processing drives substantial manual work.

↗

What it means

A reliable presorting layer can route routine cases quickly, surface exceptions deliberately, and retain a clear review path for people.

Strategic point

Automation is not a replacement for oversight: it makes the initial decision more scalable, while preserving the controls needed for supplier-change governance.

02
The current SCN process

Supplier change notifications follow five governed steps—from receipt to change and close.

IQMS documents and tracks SCNs across the process. FLASH focuses on the first three steps, creating a governed entry and routing layer before downstream impact assessment and closure activities begin.

FLASH automates the first three steps of the current SCN process.

The current process runs from receiving the supplier change notification through pre-evaluation, lead and team definition, impact assessment, and close. FLASH focuses on the front of this process: creating a governed, traceable hand-off before downstream impact assessment and closure activities begin.

STEP 1

Receive SCN

Supplier or Bayer site sends or forwards the notification to the central SQM mailbox.

STEP 2

Pre-evaluate & route

Assess relevance, identify older versions or duplicates, and route relevant SCNs into IQMS.

STEP 3

Define SCNM, lead & team

Establish the SCN manager, lead record and connected roles for the record.

STEP 4

Assess impact

Initial, site and final impact assessments remain in the downstream SCN process.

STEP 5

Change & close

Finalize the SCN record and complete change application activities where required.

Boundary by design: FLASH supports and automates steps 1–3; the subsequent impact-assessment and change-and-close steps remain governed business activities.
FLASH solution

FLASH turns the first three SCN steps into a controlled automation flow.

Power Automate orchestrates the flow. MGA-LLM extracts and evaluates information for the initial presort; IQMS is used for relevant SCNs. Cases that do not meet confidence or processing conditions remain visible and are directed to human handling.

01 · INTAKE

Supplier email arrives

Central receipt in the Bayer Pharma SCN mailbox.

02 · SORT

Identify the supplier

Power Automate checks sender information and routes the defined top-six supplier scope into presorting.

03 · EXTRACT

MGA-LLM presorts

Document and field parsing, semantic matching, extraction and confidence scoring support relevance classification.

04 · CREATE / UPDATE

Relevant SCN to IQMS

For relevant supplier change notifications, the workflow creates or updates the SCN record through the IQMS integration.

05 · CONTROL

Exception handling

AI failure, duplicates, updated versions or unclear outcomes are captured for review and root-cause investigation.

Not relevant / duplicate / updatedStored in defined email subfolders, with manual record-log and team-definition support where required.
AI cannot decidePower Automate invokes exception handling and places the email in the designated human-review path.
Control by design

All processing outcomes have a traceable destination: IQMS for relevant SCNs, categorized folders for non-relevant outcomes, and a controlled human-review route for exceptions.

What to watch for

06
Technical AI enablement

Power Automate connects the parent flow to MyGenAssist through a reusable AI child flow.

The child flow transfers the file to the designated knowledge-base folder, makes it available for the AI workflow, monitors workflow completion and returns the extracted outcome to the main Power Automate flow for record keeping. The supplier and file are the required inputs; the output remains subject to the defined validation and exception route.

Power Automate → MyGenAssist child-flow sequence

01

Receive and qualify the PDF

The main Power Automate flow triggers the child flow with the required file and supplier, then prepares the response path back to the main flow.

02

Place the file in the AI workspace

The child flow confirms the relevant knowledge-base folder, transfers the file and makes it available for viewing and workflow processing. Access and token handling remain governed implementation controls.

03

Trigger and monitor the AI workflow

The flow starts the AI workflow with file and supplier input, then retrieves workflow-run and job status details. The AI workflow confirms the supplier before invoking the appropriate supplier-specific agent; the source notes this can be streamlined into one scalable LLM agent.

04

Return, record and manage exceptions

After the workflow run and job details are available, the child flow initializes its outcome with the received output, transfers the final result to the main flow for record keeping, monitors errors and invokes the defined error path where required. The workflow end node saves output for separate extraction by the calling flow.

Get knowledge base
Upload & view file
Workflow run
Get job & run details

✓Security considerations

The connection design should use approved secret storage and should assess secure inputs/outputs, data classification, retention and access permissions before deployment.

✓Outcome controls

The receiving flow should validate the returned outcome and route uncertain, incomplete or unsupported cases through the defined review path.

✓Record-keeping considerations

The main flow can retain the returned outcome and relevant workflow status for record keeping, while avoiding unnecessary credentials or sensitive payloads.

✓Run and error monitoring

The child flow retrieves job and workflow-run details, monitors errors in the returned outcome and triggers the established error route when needed.

How Power Automate uses Veeva Vault data to route and assign an SCN

The proposed Vault interaction separates lookup, qualification matching and assignment so each routing decision is based on existing SCN and supplier qualification data.

Proposed Veeva REST API pattern
01 · CAPTURE

Prepare the request

Extract the email subject, article number(s), body and original attachment. Split comma-separated article numbers and initialize the routing result.

02 · AUTHENTICATE

Create a Vault session

Power Automate posts the required form-encoded authentication request, then uses the returned session identifier in subsequent authorized requests.

03 · SEARCH

Check for an existing SCN

Query the SCN title using the subject text. If a match exists, return the SCN identifier, record owner and SCN manager contacts to the calling flow.

04 · MATCH

Resolve qualification context

For no existing SCN, query qualification records using manufacturer and supplier article numbers. Where multiple records exist, apply the documented selection rule.

05 · RESOLVE, NOTIFY & ASSIGN

Prepare the ownership route

The proposed pattern resolves Vault user IDs, notifies the intake route with the attachment, then creates or finds the SCN and adds record owner and SCN manager roles.

Lookup and qualification matching

The source pattern uses a GET /api/v25.3/query?q=... request for an existing SCN title and qualification search. Qualification results are combined; Central Material Qualification with category 1 is preferred when several matches are returned.

Record creation and team assignment

The proposed source pattern would send the attachment to Vault intake, wait before retrieving the new record ID, then call the assignment endpoint with CSV content to add record_owner__c and scn_manager__c.

Implementation boundary: The Power Automate and MGA integration described here is a proposed technical pattern. The live endpoint, authentication headers, PDF support, request/response schema, permissions and connector policy require confirmation and testing before production use.
Architecture implication

If validated, a reusable child flow could scale AI capability through one governed integration point, consistent validation and a predictable return path for every supplier route.

The executive conclusion

FLASH AI makes supplier-change intake faster to act on—without removing the people who safeguard the process.

The future state is a transparent operating flow: relevant SCNs enter IQMS, non-relevant items are categorized, and uncertainty is surfaced for human review rather than hidden in an inbox.

EfficiencyFocus manual effort on decisions and exceptions rather than repetitive email sorting.
IntegrityMaintain human validation, exception handling and auditability throughout the flow.
ScalabilityUse the Pharma SQM pilot as a disciplined foundation for broader adoption.
